Re-review against rebased base 4813f1c5a: VERDICT=BLOCK (exit 1). Not claimed, no code written. The blocking finding is correct and I reproduced its mechanism.

review-plan --status before the re-run: {"ok": false, "verdict": "stale-code", "reason": "1 dependency file(s) changed (tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py)", "verified_at_sha": "c72b8e34ca..."} exit 12. The re-run bound to verified_at_sha 4813f1c5ad4b2b53d06bc1d1f5b3b95a8fbe25a5 (correct new base), 1 blocking + 1 advisory, signature.signed=false reason=BLOCK.

BLOCKING (G1G2, severity critical, id ff519b14f71158ff9): membership breaks two consumer tests the plan's Scope omits. Mechanically confirmed by running the tree:
  TODAY:  split_provider_qualifier('test:FunctionModel') == ('test', 'FunctionModel'); infer_provider('test:FunctionModel') == 'test'
  UNDER MEMBERSHIP: 'test' not in the 25 names -> (None, 'test:FunctionModel'); no _PROVIDER_PREFIXES entry matches -> infer_provider returns None
Path: src/rebar/llm/runner.py:596 stamps provider=infer_provider(ran_model). Breaks tests/unit/test_usage_log.py:330 (assert rows[0]['provider'] == 'test') and tests/unit/test_usage_log_failed_calls.py:121 (assert row['provider'] == 'test'). Both pass today: 28 passed baseline.
Blast radius independently verified as EXACTLY those two files — grep for a provider=='test' assertion across tests/ returns only those two lines; the three sibling files using 'test:' literals (test_code_review_step_model_attribution.py, test_code_review_usage_attribution.py, test_subcall_class_selection.py) contain no provider assertion at all. The reviewer's scope claim is precise.

WHY I STOPPED rather than remediating: the fix needs edits outside my assigned file budget (both usage_log test files; runner.py, which owns the call site, belongs to another agent), and it means rewriting PRE-EXISTING passing assertions — the explicit stop signal in my brief. Also remediation.eligible=false (within_window=false), so this needs a plan edit plus a full re-review, not a cheap re-sign.

An inconsistency in the plan worth deciding at the same time: the plan grandfathers 'google_genai' into the set specifically because a test pins it, while refusing the same treatment to 'test' — and 'test' turns out to be pinned by two tests. Both names are unusable at construction. The plan's stated rule ('the union of three sources, and nothing else') already carries one exception; whether it carries two, or zero plus assertion updates, is the open decision.

ITEM 4 — is google_genai membership genuinely required? YES, by exactly one assertion, and it does preserve an unusable value. tests/unit/test_provider_qualifier.py:72 is the parametrize case 'google_genai:gemini-2.0' feeding test_an_already_qualified_string_is_returned_unchanged (line 75). Body line 76 sets provider='google_genai'; line 77 asserts _resolve_target(already, provider) == already — with google_genai absent from the set this RAISES LLMConfigError from the new configured-provider validation, so the test fails. Line 79 (_resolve_target(already, None)) would still pass: it falls back to unqualified and no inference prefix matches 'google_genai:gemini-2.0', so it returns verbatim. So membership is load-bearing for line 77 only. And the value is unusable: ProviderSession.is_resolvable('google_genai') is False; provider_factory raises unknown provider 'google_genai'.

Verified-correct cites (all of the original brief's line numbers now match this base exactly): config.py:39 import re (sole use is :192), :169 _PROVIDER_PREFIXES, :192 _PROVIDER_QUALIFIER_RE, :195 def split_provider_qualifier, :203 the regex test, :213 infer_provider's call to split_provider_qualifier; model_classes.py:224 _resolve_target with calls at :239/:251; providers.py:54 _pydantic_ai_known_providers, :106 _builders, :118 conditional openai, :180 unknown-provider error. The plan's 24-name pydantic-ai list matches the runtime set exactly (0 symmetric difference). config.py is 681 LOC against the 800 cap, so the frozenset fits. Only surviving cite discrepancy: none.

Also confirmed no regression risk from the configured-provider validation itself: the only provider values configured anywhere in tests/ or src/ are anthropic, bedrock, openai (plus 'jira', an unrelated identity mapping) — all members.
